evidence_summary: UMI's own product census lists the Wa Pedal; a surviving 1969 example has an original CTS pot dated to week 18 of 1969. A separate catalog source describes a rare 1970s UMI Wa. The enclosure similarity to Fox Wa is retained as a comparison only, not proof of shared manufacture.

physical_builder_candidate: fOXX / Foxx founder Steve Ridinger lineage
evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the Fox Wa Pedal as related to the UMI Wa primarily because at least the enclosure is the same. This is insufficient to assign Fox Wa to UMI production or vice versa. The Fox/Foxx branch is retained as a separate builder network.
Effects Database places Apollo No. 843 inside the UMI-produced Buzz Box & Volume Expander family alongside Conrad and UMI. This is treated as a marketed-label state, not as a separate factory.

Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander is grouped with Apollo No. 843 and UMI Buzz Tone as UMI-made variants in the documented family. The archival record keeps Conrad distinct as a marketed identity while sharing builder attribution.

UMI Buzz Tone is directly identified as a U.S.-produced UMI product and is explicitly related to earlier Kimberly/Applied versions plus Apollo and Conrad marketed states. This supports a production family without collapsing separate builder periods.
UMI's product census includes the Tone Booster. The archival record continues to treat it as a separate UMI model rather than assuming it is part of the Kimberly/Applied Buzz Box lineage.

A surviving UMI Treble-Bass Booster & Mute is identified as a U.S.-made 1960s pedal. The evidence supports UMI manufacture and period placement, but exact production chronology is less secure than for the 1969 Wa and Buzz Tone records.
